world.setting: Lilyale Foundation Center — a high-security psychiatric rehabilitation facility marketed as luxury treatment but operating as a gilded prison. Huge black metal gates, armed guards, keypad-locked doors, dusty library.
world.register: clinical-psychological analysis of dark romance mechanics

avery.name: Avery
avery.role: Protagonist — young woman with severe PTSD and BPD, placed in Lilyale after killing her father. Burn scars on her arm, scarred back from a bottle attack. Hypervigilant, flinches at touch. Her nervous system has been rewired by chronic trauma.
avery.look: Early 20s woman, slight build, long dark hair often falling over her face, pale skin with visible burn scars on her forearm, wears institutional grey clothing — loose sweatshirt and joggers, haunted watchful eyes

gray.name: Gray
gray.role: Antagonist/love interest — calculating predator who reads Avery's trauma like a blueprint. Uses intermittent reinforcement: alternates devastating tenderness with violent control. Called 'demon boy'. Possessive, witty, dangerous.
gray.look: Mid 20s man, tall and imposing, sharp angular features, dark intense eyes, dark hair pushed back, wears fitted dark clothing — black henley and dark trousers, a scar or tattoo visible on his hands, radiates controlled menace

theo.name: Theo
theo.role: Another dangerous inmate who offers Avery a genuine, non-transactional connection. Tattoos over her burn scars as an act of reclaiming her bodily autonomy. Catalyst for the breaking point — his presence fractures Gray's control.
theo.look: Mid 20s man, massive imposing build, dark skin, close-cropped hair, tattoos covering both arms, wears institutional clothing but with rolled-up sleeves showing ink, gentle eyes contrasting his intimidating frame

drsmith.name: Dr. Smith
drsmith.role: Avery's assigned psychiatrist. Sterile clinical approach — asks textbook BPD questions, reads off a clipboard. His polite structured method is a language Avery's nervous system does not speak. Contrast to Gray's intuitive predatory reading of her.
drsmith.look: Middle-aged man, average build, neat grey-streaked hair, wire-rimmed glasses, wears a white lab coat over a dress shirt and tie, carries a clipboard, professional and detached demeanor

sam.name: Sam
sam.role: Hostile inmate at Lilyale. Inherently aggressive. Gray violently defends Avery from him. Theo permanently tattoos a fist onto his face as punishment.
sam.look: Young man, stocky aggressive build, shaved head, scarred knuckles, wears stained institutional clothes, perpetual sneer

saoon.name: Saoon
saoon.role: Inmate dealing with extreme bipolar swings and the recent suicide of her brother. Part of the hostile environment that pushes Avery toward isolation.
saoon.look: Young woman, thin and fragile, dark circles under her eyes, dark curly hair often unkempt, wears oversized institutional clothing, alternates between manic energy and hollow stillness

everyman.name: Everyman
everyman.role: Abstract stand-in for the reader/viewer — the one rooting for the villain, the one whose nervous system is being hacked by the narrative.
everyman.look: Androgynous figure, average build, neutral features, muted earth-tone clothing

lilyale.look: High-security psychiatric facility — huge black metal gates, armed guards, keypad-coded doors, clinical fluorescent hallways, institutional grey walls

library.look: Dusty, dimly lit library inside Lilyale — Avery's only safe space, wooden shelves, worn armchairs, diffused amber light filtering through frosted windows

averyRoom.look: Sparse institutional bedroom — single metal bed, barred window, grey blanket, harsh overhead light with no personal belongings

commonArea.look: Lilyale common room — plastic furniture bolted to the floor, buzzing fluorescent lights, tension-heavy atmosphere, other inmates scattered

therapyOffice.look: Dr. Smith's sterile consultation room — a desk, two chairs, clipboard on the table, neutral art on the wall, impersonal and clinical

gates.look: Lilyale exterior — imposing black metal gates, guard booth, gravel driveway, institutional building looming behind, grey sky

psyche.look: Abstract psychological space — representing the inner workings of the nervous system, intermittent reinforcement loops, the Skinner box

objects.why: Recurring metaphor: the gilded prison of Lilyale, psychological bondage, trauma trapping Avery
Gray's constructed persona — devotion masking possession. 'The mask cracks' is a pivotal narrative moment
The fourth wall as a mirror: reader's own reactions reflected back. Self-recognition
Central to the body-vs-mind conflict: heart racing from fear AND arousal, the physiological betrayal
Avery's medical file, Dr. Smith's clinical approach, BPD/PTSD diagnoses, the asylum setting
Avery's defense mechanisms, her safe space (library), her walls against intimacy
Keypad-locked doors at Lilyale, the exits being systematically removed, 'boarding up the windows'
Gray as the puppet master — pulling strings through intermittent reinforcement
The dark reflection — who Gray really is beneath the charm, the monster behind the mask
Avery's burn scars — the literal marks of her prior trauma, the fire of desire
The dopamine spike — unpredictable reward creating compulsive fixation, the nervous system being zapped
The systematic narrowing of Avery's world — isolation architecture funneling her toward Gray

signatureObjects.name: Skinner Box
signatureObjects.why: The variable ratio reward schedule is THE central metaphor — a lever-and-pellet mechanism that explains Gray's intermittent reinforcement strategy. The narration spends 5+ minutes on Skinner's rat experiment. No shared icon depicts an experimental box with a lever.

signatureObjects.name: Tattoo Needle
signatureObjects.why: Theo's tattoo machine is the instrument of bodily autonomy reclamation — he covers Avery's burn scars without demanding anything. It's the pivotal non-transactional act that fractures Gray's control. No shared icon depicts a tattoo gun.

signatureObjects.name: Slot Machine
signatureObjects.why: The narration explicitly compares Gray's intermittent reinforcement to a slot machine — the gambler who can't leave because the casino has 'boarded up the windows'. Used alongside the Skinner box as the human-scale version of the same trap.

spine.claim: Avery arrives at Lilyale already wired for danger — her chronic trauma has rebuilt her nervous system so that hypervigilance feels like safety and calm feels like a predator hiding.
Gray exploits the most addictive behavioral loop in existence — intermittent reinforcement — alternating devastating tenderness with violent control so Avery's dopamine system locks onto him.
The isolation architecture is complete: physical quarantine plus psychological dependence plus the body's betrayal of arousal mean Avery cannot distinguish captivity from intimacy.
The reader discovers they are inside the same Skinner box — rooting for the villain, turning pages compulsively, unable to judge Avery without judging their own pleasure.
There is no clean rescue or redemption — Macca refuses the genre's comfortable exit, leaving the nervous system permanently entangled with the predator.
